title: Any client account can read the full customer records (contact details, national ID, address, card digits)
summary: GET /api/admin/customers is documented as admin-only but returns HTTP 200 with every company's contact name, email, phone, national ID, address and card last-4 to client accounts from two different companies.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (a client)
GET /api/admin/customers (see evidence for the exact request and curl)
Observe HTTP 200 with all customers
Repeat as bright-1 (a different company): same result
actual: HTTP 200 with every customer's personal data (both clients, reproduced on re-run)
suspected_cause: The customers route checks for a signed-in user but not for the admin role (the reports route does check it)

regression_test.description: GET /api/admin/customers as a client and expect 403

plain.title: Any customer can see every other customer's personal and payment details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that feeds the Admin Portal's Customers page)
plain.what_happens: A signed-in customer account can ask for the customer list and gets back everyone's contact details, national ID number, address and card digits.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer company; the business's data-protection obligations.
plain.expected: Customers are refused; only staff can see this list.

title: A client can open another company's order by its id
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns 200 with the full order to clients of other companies, although the spec says other companies' orders must answer 404. The list endpoint is correctly filtered.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 and place an order (reference QA-ISO-1); note its id
Sign in as bright-1 (different company) and GET /api/orders/<id>
Observe HTTP 200 and the order contents
Repeat as zain-1: same result
expected: HTTP 404 for orders of another company
actual: HTTP 200 with the other company's order (2 of 2 runs, two different foreign clients)
suspected_cause: The order detail handler does not compare the order's company with the caller's company

regression_test.description: Client B GETs client A's order and expects 404

plain.title: A customer can open another company's order by changing the order number
plain.where: Behind the screens, and the order page of the Client Portal
plain.what_happens: If a customer knows or guesses another company's order id, they can read that order's items, prices and totals.
plain.who_is_affected: All customer companies; their commercial confidentiality.
plain.expected: The other company's order is reported as not found.

title: Signing out does not end the session: the token keeps working
summary: After POST /auth/logout (204) or clicking Sign out in the Client Portal, the same token still gets 200 from /me and /orders.
steps: Sign in as bright-1 over the API
POST /api/auth/logout and get 204
GET /api/me with the same token
Observe HTTP 200 (also /orders). In the Client Portal: sign in as acme-1, copy the session token in the page, click Sign out, call /api/me with it: 200
actual: HTTP 200; the token works until it expires
suspected_cause: Logout does not add the token to a revocation list

regression_test.description: Log in, log out, then GET /me with the token and expect 401

plain.title: Signing out does not actually end the session
plain.where: Behind the screens, affecting both the Client and Admin Portals
plain.what_happens: After a user signs out, their old session key still works for up to 15 minutes, so anyone holding it can keep reading data.
plain.who_is_affected: Anyone using a shared or lost device, and the company's security promise.
plain.expected: Signing out ends the session at once.

title: Tax is calculated on the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the tax is 10% of the undiscounted subtotal, so customers are overcharged. Order of 60 x $18.99 shows tax $113.94, total $1,196.37; the rules give tax $108.24, total $1,190.67. Orders below 1,000 are correct.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
New order: reference QA-UI-1, Heavy Duty Stapler, quantity 60, Place order
Confirmation says Total: $1,196.37; the order detail shows Discount -$56.97 and Tax $113.94
Same via API: POST /api/orders 80 x p-102 gives subtotal 100000, discount 5000, tax 10000, total 105000 (expected tax 9500, total 104500)
expected: Tax = 10% of (subtotal - discount); total 119067 cents for the UI order
actual: Tax = 10% of the subtotal; total 119637 cents (every order with a discount is too high by 5% of 10% of the subtotal)
suspected_cause: Tax computed from the subtotal rather than subtotal minus discount in the pricing function

regression_test.description: Order with subtotal 100000 expects tax 9500 and total 104500

plain.title: Orders over 1,000 are charged too much tax
plain.where: Client Portal order confirmation and order pages, Admin Portal orders and reports
plain.what_happens: When the 5% discount applies, tax is still worked out on the price before the discount. A $1,139.40 order shows $1,196.37 instead of $1,190.67.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer placing an order of 1,000 or more, and the sales figures.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal and open New order
Choose Heavy Duty Stapler, quantity 60, and place the order
Compare the total shown ($1,196.37) with the correct $1,190.67
plain.expected: Tax is charged only on the discounted amount.

title: The API accepts invalid order quantities and empty orders
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for quantity 0, -3, 1001, 1.5 and for an order with no items, producing negative or zero totals (a -3 quantity order shows a total of -$21.45 in both portals).
steps: Sign in as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items quantity -3 (see evidence for the request)
Observe HTTP 201; repeat with 0, 1001, 1.5 and items: []
The negative order appears in My Orders and the admin Orders list
expected: HTTP 400: whole number 1 to 1000, at least one item
actual: HTTP 201 and the order is stored
suspected_cause: Quantity and items checks are missing server-side

regression_test.description: POST quantities 0, -3, 1001, 1.5 and empty items; expect 400

plain.title: Orders with zero, negative, huge or no items are accepted
plain.what_happens: The system accepts an order for minus three items, which gives a negative total that shows in both portals and the sales figures.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff reading orders and the sales report; anyone calling the system directly.
plain.expected: Such orders are refused with a clear message.

title: Order list shows a stale status after an admin changes it
summary: After an admin moves an order to Processing, the order detail shows Processing but the order list (My Orders, and the list API) keeps showing Placed for the whole company.
steps: As acme-1 place an order QA-STALE-1 and read the list (warm)
As admin PATCH the order status to processing
As acme-1 GET the order: processing; GET /orders?q=QA-STALE-1: still placed
UI: Client Portal My Orders still shows Placed for QA-UI-1 while its detail shows Processing, also for acme-2
actual: The list is stale (it self-corrected in neither check within the run)
suspected_cause: List responses are cached per company and not cleared on a status change

regression_test.description: Warm list, PATCH status, re-read list; expect the new status

plain.title: My Orders can keep showing an old status after staff update an order
plain.what_happens: Staff move an order to Processing, the order page shows it, but the My Orders list still says Placed.
how_to_see_it: Open My Orders as a client and note an order's status
Have an admin change that order's status
Reload My Orders and compare with the order page
plain.expected: The list shows the new status.

title: Order list search and page size crash the server for some inputs
summary: GET /api/orders?q=( or q=\ and page_size=0 return HTTP 500, and page_size=-1 returns 200 with page_size -1. The Admin Portal search box shows an error when typing ( .
steps: Sign in as acme-1 (or admin)
GET /api/orders?q=(  then ?q=\  then ?page_size=0
Observe HTTP 500
In the Admin Portal Orders page type ( in Search and press Enter: error in console, no results
expected: Searches treated as plain text; invalid page_size gives 400
actual: 500 server error for q=( , q=\ and page_size=0; page_size=-1 accepted
suspected_cause: The search text is used as a regular expression without escaping; page_size is not range-checked

regression_test.description: GET /orders with q=( and page_size=0/-1 and expect no 500

plain.title: Searching orders for some characters breaks the page
plain.where: Admin Portal Orders search and the order lists
plain.what_happens: Typing a bracket or backslash into the search box makes the system fail instead of showing no results.
how_to_see_it: Open Orders in the Admin Portal
Type ( into Search and press Enter

title: Malformed requests return a stack trace and internal server file paths
summary: Invalid JSON sent to /auth/login or /orders returns 400 whose body includes a stack trace and the server's file system paths, contradicting the spec.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with body {"broken":
Observe 400 with error.trace containing file paths
Repeat on POST /api/orders
actual: error.trace with stack trace and source paths
suspected_cause: The JSON parse error handler returns the stack

regression_test.description: Send malformed JSON and assert no trace or path in the body

plain.title: Error messages reveal internal details of the server
plain.what_happens: A badly formed request makes the system answer with technical internals such as file locations.
plain.who_is_affected: The company's security; it helps attackers.

title: Admin sales report takes about 4 seconds to load
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales consistently takes about 4 seconds; the Reports page is blank until it finishes.
steps: Sign in as admin
GET /api/admin/reports/sales
Observe about 4000 ms, twice
Admin Portal Reports shows only the title for several seconds
suspected_cause: Slow aggregation or an artificial delay in the report

plain.title: The Reports page is slow
plain.what_happens: The sales summary takes about four seconds to appear and the page looks empty meanwhile.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Admin Portal and open Reports
Wait for the figures to appear
plain.expected: The summary appears quickly or shows a loading message.

title: My Orders on a phone: the filter bar covers the first order and the total and View link are cut off
summary: At 390px wide the Status filter and New order button overlap the first row, and the table is wider than the screen so the total is clipped and the View link is off-screen with no cue.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Resize to 390x844 and open My orders
Observe the first order row hidden under the filter bar, totals cut off
Reload: same (audit lists the covered row)
actual: First row covered; total and View clipped (table 457px in a 359px box)
suspected_cause: Sticky or fixed toolbar and a fixed-width table without responsive layout

regression_test.description: At 390px width the orders table has no covered rows

plain.title: My Orders is hard to use on a phone
plain.what_happens: On a phone the filter bar sits on top of the newest order and the total and View link are cut off.
how_to_see_it: Open My Orders on a phone or narrow window (390 wide)
Look at the first order and the right-hand columns
plain.expected: Every order and column can be seen and tapped.

title: Some form controls have no label for screen readers
area: Admin Orders search and filters; Client New order
summary: The Admin Orders search box has only a placeholder, the refresh and clear-filter icon buttons have no name, and the product dropdown on the Client New order page has no label.
steps: Sign in as admin, open Orders, run the page audit
Observe unnamed search input and two icon buttons (desktop and mobile)
Client Portal New order: the product select is unnamed
expected: Every control has an accessible name

regression_test.description: Accessibility check that every input and button has a name

plain.title: Some buttons and fields cannot be understood by screen readers
plain.where: Admin Portal Orders page; Client Portal New order page
plain.what_happens: The search box, two small icon buttons and the product dropdown have no name.

title: Urdu text is not marked right-to-left
area: Client My Orders and Admin Customers
summary: Urdu references and the Urdu company name sit in left-to-right, left-aligned cells; the pages have no dir attribute.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as zain-1 and view My orders
Audit lists the three Urdu references as Urdu in an LTR container
Admin Customers lists the Urdu company name the same way
expected: Urdu text displayed with right-to-left direction

regression_test.description: Urdu cells have dir=auto or rtl

plain.title: Urdu text is laid out as if it were English
plain.where: Client Portal My Orders; Admin Customers
plain.what_happens: Urdu order names and company names are aligned left, which can look wrong or scramble numbers.
how_to_see_it: Sign in as the Urdu customer and open My Orders
plain.expected: Urdu text reads right to left.
